title: Isao stops printing rock where the kit walls belong: a grown base read its unprinted rim as twelve breaches and repaired them before the gate
context: Owner, playtesting the published V1 on the bare index.html: 'When Isao starts to build at the beginning of story mode, he builds ROCKS instead of WALLS, in the phase before building the gate.' The base now grows in play (2026-09-16-isao-grows-the-base): the programme's first step is the gate and its twelve walls, and src/fx/story-base.js holds the pending kit WALL instances at zero scale until Isao prints them.
outcome: The cause was the repair rule's caller, not the print and not the lattice. story.wallCells (src/platform/story-world.js:118) is the PENDING wall cells, which are open FLOOR until the gate step stands; storyApi.build() in src/td-tab.js fed them straight to nextRepair as 'cells that should be rock and are not', so at the landing a grown base reported eleven holes and Isao flew out to 'repair' a rim that had never been built. Each repair ran storyApi.repaired(): it tagged the cell BLOCKED in dungeon.tags and tdFullTags and called rebuildAfterBreach(), so board-surface.refreshCells() drew a ROCK top there, and storyBase.restoreWall() snapped a single kit WALL segment to full scale. That is the rock the owner watched rise before the gate. Fix: in storyApi.build() the repair scan (gate and walls alike) runs only once the gate step stands - programmeHas(pg, 'gate'), the perk the gate-and-walls step carries, which a static stage-4 base already holds from its first frame through makeBuildProgramme's standing() - and state().programme.broke reports 0 until then. Isao now prints the gate and the kit walls as their models and storyApi.printed() alone turns the rim to rock, exactly as the static base has it at load. src/td-tab.js stays at 13506 lines (net 0; both edits are inside existing one-liners), so the budget in docs/architecture-budget.json holds.
alternatives: Stop the lattice drawing ROCK at printed wall cells (the reported hypothesis). REJECTED by evidence: the static stage-4 base does exactly the same tagging - src/platform/story-world.js:83 blocks every non-pending wall cell at load - and both plans produce the identical wall cells, so stage 4 stands with those six lattice cells as rock under its kit walls and the owner has never complained about that look. Suppressing the rock would have made the grown base diverge from the static one and would have left the tank and the swarm walking through the rim.

Widen story.wallCells to every wall cell rather than only the pending ones, so a static stage-4 rim can also be repaired. Left alone: it is a separate gap in the repair feature, not this bug, and it would change stage-4 behaviour during a playtest.
Gate the repair scan on a wave/phase test instead of the programme perk. Rejected: the perk is the same signal the static path uses for a step that already stands, so one rule covers both bases.
evidence: Before, src/td-tab.js at 0b1aa589, grown page index.html?sw=0&acceptance=1&cine=0&world=story&threat=0.35&heart=none&stage=1&grow=1#td: at the landing state().programme reported broke=11 and repairing={kind:'wall',ci:30555} with printed=[] - repairs on a rim that had never been printed.

Before: state().wallCount rose 43009 -> 43015 BEFORE the gate step became active at 70.4 s, and the gate print (k 0.046 -> 1) then added nothing. 43015 is exactly the static stage-4 wall count, so the phantom repairs had already laid the whole rim as rock. artifacts/qa/isao-walls/timeline.json.

The static path tags the same cells: node scripts/architecture.mjs aside, test/world-recipe.mjs asserts 'Story world composition blocks wall cells and keeps the gate open', and a Node comparison of planBase(planet, layout, 4) against planBase(planet, layout, 1, {reach: 8}) showed identical wall cells (12 segments on 6 distinct lattice cells), all open floor inside the clearing before either path blocks them.

After, same script and page: at the landing state().programme reported broke=0 and repairing=null; state().wallCount held 43009 through the whole gate print (k 0.082 -> 0.982) and rose to 43015 only as printed('gate') fired at k=1 - the rim turns to rock when the walls stand, not before. The gate step also began at 39.2 s instead of 70.4 s, the six phantom repair trips gone, and the run logged no console errors. artifacts/qa/isao-walls-after/timeline.json.

Screenshots from the same camera (state().focusHeart) at the moment the gate-and-walls step finishes: artifacts/qa/isao-walls/B5-after-gate-focus.jpg (before) and artifacts/qa/isao-walls-after/B5-after-gate-focus.jpg (after).

npm test: 120 test programs passed. npm run check: syntax, source module identity, pinned kernel, logs and assets checked. npm run architecture: game/lab controller boundaries, line budgets and top-level placement hold (src/td-tab.js 13506 lines, unchanged).

scripts/browser-lock.sh node scripts/browser-test.mjs --grow after the fix: exit 0, every step PASS (grow-bare, grow-landing, grow-gate-printing, grow-tremor, grow-fodder, grow-settled, grow-study, grow-solar-rising, grow-bays, grow-hugin, grow-finished). The block after 'gate stands' asserts walls0 < wallCount <= walls0 + 12, the rise the phantom repairs used to defeat by laying the whole rim as rock before the step began.
scripts/browser-lock.sh node scripts/browser-test.mjs --story-world after the fix: exit 0, 31 steps PASS, story-world-rotor-kill included.
